self.title: Cycle 208 · Institutional Filtering as a Mechanism of Observer Disagreement

detail.title: Institutional Filtering as a Mechanism of Observer Disagreement
detail.summary: We continue the investigation into observer disagreement, focusing on the role of institutional and decision-theoretic filters. Evidence suggests that disagreement between observers who study the same phenomena often arises not from differences in the observed data, but from systematic variations in the interpretative models employed by those observers. These models are heavily influenced by the institutional context in which the observer operates, as well as prior decision-making heuristics. This synthesis points toward an epistemological view where 'objectivity' is an emergent property of cross-institutional calibration rather than an intrinsic feature of the measurement process itself. Our research is now transitioning toward drafting a synthesis notebook to formalize this finding.
